title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
text:
Challenges

Currently: classical supervised learning with deep learning models (PyTorch)

Frugal, performant and fast, production-ready… 😎
… but requires between 100k and 1M labelled data points 🫨

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
section: MLOps: facilitated by Onyxia, but still incomplete
text:
MLOps: facilitated by Onyxia, but still incomplete

Data: S3 storage (Datalab), versioning with MLFlow Datasets ✅
Model: in-house development and distribution via torchTextClassifiers, parallelised training with Argo Workflows, model storage with MLFlow ✅
Deployment: FastAPI deployed via containerisation (Docker) ✅
Monitoring: this is where it falls short ❌

Requires human investment, not always done
How to monitor the model in production without continuous human annotation?

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
section: The need to move away from labelled data
text:
The need to move away from labelled data

What to do when labelled data is unavailable or insufficient?
What to do when the nomenclature is updated?

Existing data needs to be re-coded

What to do when our labelled data is unreliable?

and ideally we want to correct it…

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
text:
A first zero-shot approach: RAG

A first zero-shot approach: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Knowledge base = official descriptions for each code
A good first solution, but…

dependency on chunking
dependency on the embedding model
context saturation with descriptions
comparing a description embedding to a label embedding
no traceability, no reasoning
no consideration of the hierarchy!

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
text:
Objectives

No more embeddings
We want reasoning: the LLM can/must justify its choices (chain of thought)

Rather than imposing context as in a RAG, let the model complete its context dynamically (= agent!)
Ideally, with reasoning around the hierarchy

Using the graph as a foundation for agents

We define a set of tools shared by all agents:

get_code_information
get_current_children
get_current_siblings
go_to_parent
go_to_child
etc.

They all use Neo4j syntax

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
text:
The agents

An agent = a prompt, an input/output type, and tools
The closers: CodeChooser, MatchVerifier
Text2Code (classifier): the Navigator inherits from Text2Code
Code2Text (synthetic data generator)

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
text:
Evaluation

Evaluating a classifier agent

If we trust our test dataset: straightforward evaluation
Otherwise: manual evaluation!

Ground truth prediction, classifier prediction, CodeChooser and MatchVerifier judgements combined
Joint evaluation of all components


Evaluating synthetic data generation

Less straightforward
Retrain a model on a synthetic dataset and check whether equivalent performance is reached on the same test set

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
text:
Perspectives

Requirements met

No more embeddings
Reasoning and traceability
Usable for any nomenclature: just create a Neo4j database with the descriptions and everything works!

GRAAL is just a distributor of tools, prompts and LLM call structures (input/output validation)


The main task ahead is evaluation 🎯

title: GRAAL: Graph-based Research with Agents for Automatic Labelling
section: What will we do with it?
text:
What will we do with it?

An agentic model is too heavy for production (no GPU yet, inference time too high…)
However, GRAAL can be used for:

Monitoring the deployed model: MatchVerifier analyses API logs, evaluates the model continuously, calls the Navigator if re-coding is needed
Re-coding a database (same workflow as monitoring)
Synthetic data generation (Code2Text)
